title: fix(ui): keep chat and drafts usable when connections fail
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: slow or interrupted connections replace usable chat and visualizations with errors, strand message delivery, and prevent previously signed-in users from reopening their work offline.

## User Impact

Users can keep reading cached conversations, editing text and attachment drafts, and queuing messages after a connection loss or an offline reload. Recovery appears in the existing bottom-left connection indicator, not a second chat banner. Loaded widgets retain their local interaction state.

Offline reload requires a prepared browser cache and an explicit browser-offline signal. Server actions and uncached external resources still require a connection. Previously signed-in proxy, Tailscale, and password users gain local access without storing their password or new bearer credentials; sending waits for account revalidation. People with access to the browser profile can read retained local data.

**Migration:** the derived transcript cache moves from IndexedDB version 3 to 4; unscoped old history is discarded and refilled online rather than assigned to another account. Unsent legacy drafts and queues remain available for explicit recovery, never automatic reassignment or sending. Retention limits remain unchanged; rollback does not turn account-qualified input back into an unowned queue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep presentation alive independently of connection authority. Retry transient reads within their existing recovery windows, reconcile uncertain writes using the original message ID, and scope local work to its Gateway/account. Same-client account replacement, stale handoffs, cross-tab retirement, and explicit credential-forget cannot transfer another account’s input. The service worker prepares only integrity-bound build assets and a generic shell, retains native online HTTP-auth navigation, and resumes interrupted preparation without holding updates indefinitely.

The offline-access and account-isolation contract was explicitly accepted by @steipete in the linked work session.

## Evidence

- **Full UI inventory exercised: 1,605/1,605 files**, once each, on the checksum-pinned CI Bun runtime. The run recorded 23,795 passing tests, five stale retention assertions in one fixture, and one existing opt-in skip. The five assertions were corrected without changing production code; the corrected fixture and boot-owner siblings then passed **63/63 tests** with zero lint warnings/errors. The original full run is retained as-is, not relabeled green.
- **Final isolated browser suite: 133/133 tests across all 17 files passed**, with no skips. This includes real-Gateway Inspector pairing, offline/recovery fences, account-scoped drafts and attachments, queued delivery, loading deadlines, navigation, widgets, and reconnect reconciliation. Official Playwright 1.63 image; one worker; owned container positively removed.
- **Fresh production build and unchanged performance budgets passed.** Latest rebuilt startup JS: 372,295 B gzip, 52 B below the enforcement limit. Startup CSS: 50,705 B, 495 B below its hard ceiling; the existing advisory warning remains. Chat/New boot use 32/27 requests, below 35. No budget or baseline relaxed.
- **Production Chromium/SW proof passed all eight account/offline stages and four native HTTP Basic proxy stages**, with zero page errors. Offline navigation came from the service worker while a network probe failed. Original-account retention, different account/Gateway fencing, return to the original account, and “Forget this browser” were exercised. Proxy proof observed 17 native challenges and 113 authenticated asset requests.
- Production UI types and all five canonical UI test type graphs passed, with scoped typed lint, formatting, line-count and assertion-safety ratchets. All tracked source, dependency and runtime fingerprints stayed unchanged during final browser/build proof. The account/proxy proof used build 2026.9.7-64b426373e23-2026-10-01T21-06-21.168Z; build/performance checks also passed after the private-export cleanup at 53ed9b1.
- Independent review findings were reproduced and repaired. The final automated routing warning was rejected after inspecting the sole production getter and router call chain: offline defaults are null while connected, scoped to the current account/Gateway, and refreshed by live discovery; focused runtime-owner tests passed. No unresolved actionable P0–P2 finding remains. **Hosted exact-head CI/review gates are still separate requirements; local proof is not a hosted-CI or merge claim.**

- **Hosted dependency failure repaired:** the obsolete global roster-generation export is now private, its test observes the existing account-scoped getter, and an unused legacy test helper was removed. Both complete Knip scans, 44 focused tests, affected production/test type graphs and typed lint pass. No dead-code suppression or production behavior change.
- **All eight cases in four additional browser files pass in scoped runs.** Speech hydration now inspects the authenticated snapshot key; elapsed-time proof advances heartbeat callbacks chronologically and verifies one connection/send; catalog readiness keeps the same enabled-control assertion. Worker-update tests use the exact staged build-plus-digest cache, real install gate and generic shell. Instrumented reproduction established that network-isolated Chromium reported offline despite reachable loopback; a native online-state precondition preserves network isolation. The final diagnostic-free worker suite passed 4/4 in 38.96 seconds, with all draft, activation, asset-SHA and exact-one terminal-attach checks intact. No timing budgets or skips changed; WebKit was not run.

### Integration and recovery repairs

Actual conflicts with main were resolved while retaining live-only agent discovery, warm pre-hello routing, history supersession, and Mermaid 12 worker handling. Existing landed CI prerequisites remain integrated unchanged. No main refresh was performed merely to chase branch movement.

- Valid credential non-admission no longer deletes another document’s boot record. Explicit retirement, failed publication, and cross-tab cache cleanup affect only their captured owner; shellless sign-in/approval documents cannot retire an authenticated Chat tab.
- Legacy recovery uses verified inactive, account-bound staging before publishing a destination. Throwing/silent/commit-then-throw failures, source resurrection, reopened storage, different-destination retries and Blob custody are covered. Required recovery writes reject before mutation if bounded retention would drop the destination or existing unsent input; ordinary cache retention is unchanged.
- Memory-only, unconfirmed input survives A→B→A under its original opaque owner without exposing it to B or reviving stale send authority. Peer durable edits supersede dormant copies; returning in-flight input remains held for explicit action.
- All chat sends share a finite acknowledgment deadline. A real browser-client wire test keeps heartbeats healthy while withholding an approval-command ACK: at 30 seconds it restores original text/attachment bytes, reports delivery unconfirmed, preserves the active run, ignores a late ACK, and sends nothing again on reconnect.
- Production asset admission uses the canonical route selector rather than counting mutually exclusive preload templates together. Limits and integrity checks remain unchanged; type-only outbox dependencies use existing leaf owners without an import cycle.
